data.title: TPG-backed Newquest sells Rs 115-crore Shadowfax stake; Gallantt Ispat promoter offloads 0.66%
data.description:
Newquest Asia Fund, owned by global private equity firm TPG, sold nearly Rs 115 crore worth of shares in Shadowfax Technologies, the Bengaluru-headquartered third-party logistics company, through open-market transactions on November 20.

The stock appeared to react to the transaction, declining 2.02 percent to Rs 307.25 after touching a record high of Rs 315.25 during the trading session.

Newquest Asia Fund IV (Singapore) offloaded 37.28 lakh equity shares in Shadowfax, representing 0.63 percent of the company's paid-up equity, for Rs 114.83 crore. The shares were sold at an average price of Rs 308 apiece.

This was the fund's second stake sale in Shadowfax during the current quarter. Earlier, on October 6, it sold 40 lakh shares, representing a 0.68 percent stake, for Rs 114.8 crore.

Following the latest transaction, Newquest Asia Fund's shareholding in the logistics company declined to around 6.04 percent from 7.35 percent at the end of September 2026.

Gallantt Ispat promoter offloads 0.66% stake

Meanwhile, Dinesh R Agarwal, promoter of Gallantt Ispat, sold another 16.1 lakh equity shares in the iron and steel producer, equivalent to 0.66 percent of its total paid-up equity, for Rs 84.36 crore. The shares were sold at an average price of Rs 523.93 apiece.

On the other side of the transaction, Shree Surabhi Flour Mills acquired 5.5 lakh shares for Rs 28.76 crore at Rs 523 apiece, while Suryalaxmi Infracon purchased 10.6 lakh shares for Rs 55.6 crore at Rs 524.41 apiece.

With Friday's transaction, Dinesh Agarwal has sold a total of 1.36 crore equity shares, representing a 5.64 percent stake, during the current quarter. This is against the 5.81 percent stake held by him, as per the latest shareholding pattern.

Meanwhile, Suryalaxmi Infracon has acquired 1.06 crore shares, representing 4.4 percent of Gallantt Ispat's paid-up equity, during the current quarter.

Gallantt Ispat shares ended at Rs 538.10 on the National Stock Exchange, down 0.16 percent.

data.title: Flesh-eating screwworm cases surge in US, keeping ranchers on alert
data.description:
Key points:
  • USDA confirmed 149 screwworm cases in domestic animals since June
  • Warm, wet weather encouraged pest to spread this autumn
  • Screwworms likely to survive winter in parts of southwestern US
  • USDA restarted imports of Mexican cattle in August

By Tom Polansek and Heather Schlitz

US infestations of New World screwworm, a parasitic fly that eats warm-blooded animals alive and threatens the cattle herd, have surged in unusually wet and warm weather in the Southwest, the US Department of Agriculture and state veterinarians said.

Screwworms infested 64 cattle, dogs, horses and other domesticated animals this month, up from 34 in October and three in September, according to USDA data.

The agency has reported 149 total cases in domesticated animals since June, along with two in wild elk. Of those, 73 cases were active as of Thursday, up from two at the end of September.

Ranchers fear cases will continue to climb because there is a shortage of sterile flies that are bred to combat screwworm flies.

"The swarm has not reached Texas yet," said Susan Storey, a South Texas rancher.

USDA is racing to expand sterile fly production capacity, with the Army Corps of Engineers overseeing construction of a fly plant in South Texas due to open next year. USDA Under Secretary Dudley Hoskins told Reuters that a project to test genetically modified sterile flies that could potentially aid its response was progressing.

The agency first detected screwworm in a calf in Texas in June after the parasite marched north through Mexico, and later confirmed more cases in Texas and New Mexico. Following a lull, screwworms last month spread to Arizona, which now has nine active cases across four counties.

Screwworms encroached on Arizona from the south and east, said Dr. Ryan Wolker, state veterinarian. "The major contributing factor is the natural progression of the pest and the limited supply of sterile male screwworm flies," he said.

GENETICALLY ENGINEERED STERILE FLIES

USDA is releasing all available sterile flies in the southwestern US and around Mexico's northern border to contain infestations, while screwworms are still multiplying farther south. Sterile males mate with wild females, whose eggs then fail to hatch.

"There was a good bit of Mexico where we didn't have a good barrier of sterile flies to stop that natural progression," said Dr. Samantha Holeck, New Mexico's state veterinarian. "Now it's right there at the border — both sides of the border."

Researchers in Panama have made progress testing sterile flies genetically engineered to produce only males, which could give USDA an edge in the battle against screwworms, Hoskins said. The flies, known as NovoFly, could double the production of sterile flies by eliminating females, which are not useful in eradication efforts, he said.

"To date, all the signs and signals indicate progress and a strong competitiveness of the NovoFly in the wild," Hoskins said. "The tests so far have demonstrated everything we were hoping they would."

USDA intends to produce NovoFly at the facility scheduled to open in Texas in April, if testing continues to go well, Hoskins said. He added that it will take time to ramp up production.

The agency restarted cattle imports from Mexico at ports of entry in Arizona and New Mexico in August, after blocking them last year in an attempt to keep screwworms out. The halt helped push US beef prices to record highs for consumers.

The imports did not cause cases to spike because Mexican cattle are inspected multiple times for screwworm before entering the US, according to Hoskins, Wolker and Holeck.

Instead, rain linked to El Niño created favorable conditions for screwworms to spread, experts said, with Hurricanes Rachel and Polo bringing increased late-season moisture to Arizona and Mexico.

"As this spreads, it just exacerbates the need for more sterile flies," said David Anderson, agricultural economist at Texas A&M University.

This winter, temperatures will likely not drop low enough to kill screwworms in parts of Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, veterinarians said. That means ranchers, hunters and pet owners must watch closely for more cases.

"We're all nervous," said John Sewell, owner of a 40-square-mile deer-hunting ranch in South Texas. "You can only hope the USDA plan is working."

data.title: Nestle Eyes Autonomous Factory Lines and Looks to Google, Microsoft as Partners — Update
data.description:
By Aimee Look

ORBE, Switzerland--Swiss food giant Nestle is targeting autonomous factory lines in the future, as the maker of KitKat chocolates and Nescafe coffee teams up with big tech companies to deploy artificial intelligence.

The endgame? Getting factory lines to run themselves, Nestle's technology chief, Stefan Palzer, said in an interview.

"You need the big guys, who have the best capabilities, who have the best hardware and software solutions," he said, after Nestle opened a tech facility in Orbe, Switzerland, on Friday.

Nestle has signed partnership agreements with Microsoft and Boston Dynamics to develop AI and engineering solutions at its new Deep Tech facility. It is also in the final rounds of discussions with Google for a partnership, and leveraging some of Apple's spatial computing technology too, he added.

The company's eventual aim with these tech deals is to drive business growth, Palzer said.

With sensors and AI, Nestle's lines can fully understand and adapt to variable inputs and produce consistent output. Using the partnerships to develop an agentic AI workflow in the future would also be necessary to have automated lines, Palzer said, referring to the technology that can make decisions without much human supervision.

"At a certain point in time--we're not there yet--you can put agentic AI on top of it, and then it's orchestrating the entire flow," he said. "The fully autonomous line is one of the future. We will still need our experts, because we need expert judgment in most cases."

There will always be humans making decisions, Nestle's chief executive officer, Philipp Navratil, said.

To implement automated manufacturing workflows, Nestle needs to consider them category by category, Palzer said. His team is currently looking at unit operations to make them autonomous.

"We now do unit by unit, and we're focusing here on our top ten [manufacturing] processes," Palzer said. "We're not far away."

Developing factory lines for the food industry is different, for example, from other sorts of manufacturing like the car industry--where inputs are more uniform--said Judith Arfsten, who is head of Nestle's Deep Tech Center. For example, a hotter-than-usual summer can lead to completely different natural raw materials in a given time. Tech will work to enable the use of AI, smart sensors and robotics to improve operational efficiency.

Using AI is part of Nestle's broader strategy of identifying new ways to better understand changing consumer habits. Unpredictability around customer behavior is heightened due to weight-loss drugs and pressure on household budgets, and many companies in the sector are looking to AI for guidance.

A key question is how Nestle and other food companies can use innovation to actually drive sales, particularly for GLP-1 consumers, Vontobel analyst Jean-Philippe Bertschy said. "Technology can help with reformulation and product development, but execution will matter more than the tools," he said.

Partners including Microsoft and Boston Dynamics, which confirmed their cooperation, will help provide hardware and AI capabilities to improve both factory processes and consumer-facing products like coffee machines. The company also aims to advance its digital and hardware processes, and agreed with IBM in 2025 to use AI for packaging innovation.

The center in Orbe is also going to complement Nestle's work at its Shenzhen hub, where it seeks to identify Chinese tech it can use in products around the world.

data.title: COMBINED GENERAL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 20, 2026: ARGAN SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE THE MERGER WITH WDP
data.description:
Press release – Neuilly-sur-Seine, Friday, November 20, 2026 – 5.45 pm

COMBINED GENERAL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 20, 2026: ARGAN SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE THE MERGER WITH WDP

  • Approval of the cross-border merger by absorption of ARGAN into WDP, expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027
  • Approval of the exceptional distribution of €11 per share, to be paid before completion of the merger
  • Progress on the conditions precedent

At the Combined General Meeting held on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the Palais Brongniart in Paris, ARGAN shareholders approved all resolutions supported by the Management Board and the Supervisory Board, paving the way for the merger with WDP.

As of the date of the meeting, ARGAN's share capital consisted of 25,766,939 shares, representing 25,748,892 voting rights. Shareholders present, represented, having granted a proxy to the Chairman or having voted by correspondence together held 22,429,229 shares and an equal number of voting rights, representing 87.10% of the total.

Approval of all resolutions supported by ARGAN's Management Board and Supervisory Board

The Combined General Meeting approved all resolutions supported by the Supervisory Board and the Management Board, including:

  • Resolution No. 3 approving the common draft terms of the cross-border merger entered into on July 23, 2026, between ARGAN and Warehouses De Pauw NV (“WDP”), as well as the merger by absorption of ARGAN into WDP (the “Merger”), adopted with 93.11% of the votes.

Under the terms of the common draft terms of the cross-border merger, each ARGAN share will be exchanged for 3 newly issued WDP shares. Completion of the Merger, which will result in the delisting of ARGAN shares from Euronext Paris and the admission to trading of the newly issued WDP shares on Euronext Brussels, Euronext Amsterdam and Euronext Paris, is expected to take place during the first quarter of 2027, subject to the satisfaction of the remaining conditions precedent. WDP's Extraordinary General Meeting, which will be called upon to approve the Merger, will be held on November 24, 2026.

  • Resolution No. 2 approving an exceptional distribution of €11 per share, to be paid out of share premium reserves (the “Exceptional Distribution”), adopted with 97.02% of the votes.

The ex-date and payment date of the Exceptional Distribution will be determined at a later date by the Management Board and announced in a press release. The Exceptional Distribution will take place before completion of the Merger.

Progress on the conditions precedent

In addition to the approval of the Merger by ARGAN's General Meeting, the following regulatory approvals required for completion of the Merger have recently been obtained. In particular:

  • The French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques) issued a favourable tax ruling in line with the requests submitted by ARGAN and WDP;
  • The French Financial Markets Authority (Autorité des Marchés Financiers, ‘AMF’) confirmed that the transaction would not trigger a mandatory public buyout offer;
  • The Merger was approved by the relevant authorities under applicable foreign investment control regulations;
  • The Belgian Financial Services and Markets Authority (FSMA) approved the amendments to WDP's articles of association in connection with the Merger; and
  • The applicable waiting period for the European Commission's review of the Merger under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation has expired.

Completion of the Merger, which is expected to take place during the first quarter of 2027, remains subject to the other conditions precedent set out in Article 4 of the common draft terms of the cross-border merger, in particular the approval of the Merger by WDP's Extraordinary General Meeting, which will be held on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and the issuance of the pre-merger certificates in France and Belgium.

Further information on the Merger is available on the Company's website and at www.wdp-argan.eu.

The full minutes of the General Meeting held on November 20, 2026, will be available on the Company's website by the end of the day. A replay of the General Meeting is available on argan.fr via the following link: https://argan.engagestream.euronext.com/assemblee_generale_extraordinaire_2026.

data.title: Markets were overdue for a tech correction, but trade will bounce – JPMorgan’s David Kelly
data.description:
The stock market was overdue for a tech correction, according to David Kelly, JPMorgan Asset Management's chief global strategist, who pointed to Nvidia's recent problems and broader technological disruptions as key factors driving the pullback.

In an interview with CNBC, Kelly noted that the troubles have been "rattling a few people."

Despite concerns about the AI trade and slowing demand in the tech sector , , Kelly sees inflation pressures easing and little evidence of broad economic overheating.

He expects falling gasoline prices (XB1:COM) alone will reduce the year-over-year increase in CPI by four-tenths of a percent for November.

"I see no evidence that in the big, broad economy outside of tech, there's that strong demand," Kelly said, pointing to flat new housing activity and weak consumer basics.

On Federal Reserve policy, Kelly pushed back against expectations for aggressive rate hikes. He characterized Fed Governor Waller as "a lonesome poke" in his support for a 50-basis-point hike, saying he does not believe the majority of Federal Reserve officials share that view.

Kelly anticipates a move in December followed by a pause rather than continued tightening.

He also argued that markets are constructing a hawkish Fed narrative in the absence of forward guidance, but he sees no justification for aggressive action.

"With rates already as pretty close to neutral levels, there's no reason for the Federal Reserve to be aggressive here," he said.

Looking ahead, Kelly expressed optimism about market resilience. He noted that steady inflows through 401(k) contributions, stock buybacks, and purchases by wealthy Americans provide consistent support.

"Unless you have a big reason for negativity, chances are this market will bounce," he said.

data.description: Any long-term economic boost from the EU and U.K.'s reset deal will likely be small and pale in comparison with Brexit's overall hit to U.K. GDP, Oxford Economics says. data.title: Kansas City Fed Services Activity Index Falls in November
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Services activity in the middle of the U.S. slowed in November, while expectations for future activity moved higher, according to a monthly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

The Tenth District Services Survey's composite index, a weighted average of indexes covering revenue/sales, employment and inventory, came in at 3 in November, down from 10 in October but up from 0 in September. Readings above zero indicate expansion, while those below zero indicate contraction.

The Kansas City Fed said growth eased in both business and consumer services, driven by modest declines in auto and real-estate services.

The bank said its index of expectations for future services activity came in at 20 in November, up from 4 in October.

The Kansas City Fed's survey, released Friday, includes participants from such service industries as retail and wholesale trade, automobile dealers, real estate and restaurants. The survey provides information on current services activity in the Tenth District, which includes Colorado, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, the northern half of New Mexico and the western third of Missouri.

The bank's monthly manufacturing survey, released Thursday, showed that factory activity in the central U.S. rose in November.

data.title: Dolphin Drilling Completes Sale of Blackford Dolphin, Sign Joint Venture Agreement and Appoints Ronny Bjørnådal as Executive Chairman
data.description:
Oslo, 20 November 2026 – Dolphin Drilling AS (Euronext Growth Oslo: DDRIL) ("Dolphin Drilling" or the "Company") announces that it has completed the sale of the semi-submersible drilling rig "Blackford Dolphin" to Voyage Shipping Inc., a guaranteed nominee of SPM Energy Shipping FZCO ("SPM"). Reference is made to the Company’s announcement of 26 October 2026.

As previously announced, the purchase price comprised an initial cash consideration of USD 10 million, settled at closing, and a remaining consideration of USD 15 million, payable subject to receipt of the first payment under a potential future drilling contract.

Dolphin Drilling and SPM have today also entered into a joint venture agreement to pursue drilling contracts in India for "Blackford Dolphin", another rig owned by SPM and other rigs that the parties may agree. The parties are in the process of incorporating the joint venture company in India that will tender the rigs for employment and enter into drilling contracts in the country. The parties intend to establish this company as the operator for their rigs and drilling contracts in India and have a mutual commitment to primarily pursue opportunities in India through the joint venture company. Any tender jointly submitted will be subject to the prior consent of both SPM and Dolphin Drilling, and to the parties entering into a management agreement for Dolphin Drilling to provide for reactivation of the drilling unit and operations under the relevant drilling contract. SPM shall be responsible for all capital costs, operating expenses and guarantees related to future drilling contracts.

Completion of the transactions reduces the Company’s risk and capital commitments, and provides a platform for growth in rig management on a capital-light basis.

"Completing the sale of Blackford Dolphin is a milestone for Dolphin Drilling. It materially reduces our risk and capital commitments, and it marks the start of a capital-light business model where our operating platform, licences and long track record are put to work in partnership with SPM. This is an important transaction for Dolphin Drilling and a clear step in executing upon our strategy to utilize our market leading drilling platform. Together with SPM, we are well positioned to grow the number of rigs under our management and to create long-term value for our shareholders," says Ronny Bjørnådal, Executive Chairman of Dolphin Drilling.

"Blackford Dolphin and the joint venture in India is the first step in our partnership with Dolphin Drilling. By combining our commercial reach with Dolphin Drilling’s proven operating platform, we look forward to growing the fleet together," says Gaurav Mehta, Chairman of the Board of SPM.

Ronny Bjørnådal appointed Executive Chairman

The Board of Directors has appointed Ronny Bjørnådal as Executive Chairman of Dolphin Drilling, effective immediately. In this role, Mr Bjørnådal will work closely with the Board and management on the Company’s strategy and lead the work on strategic initiatives and growth opportunities, including further partnerships and opportunities to participate in industry consolidation. The day-to-day operational management of the Company will continue to be led by Michael Boyd, CEO and Johan Finnestad, COO.

"The Blackford Dolphin transaction shows that there are attractive opportunities for Dolphin Drilling in today’s market. As Executive Chairman, I will dedicate my efforts to developing our strategy and pursuing transactions that can grow the Company, broaden our platform and create value for our shareholders. There are a lot of opportunities for Dolphin Driling and I am looking forward to working with the Board and management to pursuethem," says Ronny Bjørnådal.

Background

On 26 October 2026, Dolphin Drilling announced that it had entered into a definitive sale and purchase agreement with SPM for the sale of "Blackford Dolphin" for a total consideration of up to USD 25 million, together with a memorandum of understanding for the management of "Blackford Dolphin", one additional semi-submersible drilling rig and any other rigs or units the parties may agree upon. The sale immediately and materially reduces the Company’s operating cost base and eliminates the class renewal survey capital expenditures related to "Blackford Dolphin". At the end of the second quarter of 2026, Dolphin Drilling reported total cash of USD 55.1 million and a firm contract backlog of USD 556 million, with a further USD 446 million in options, following multi-year contracts secured for "Paul B. Loyd Jr." and "Borgland Dolphin".

Solid market outlook

Dolphin Drilling continues to see a tight market for semi-submersible drilling rigs, the segment in which its fleet operates. Over several years, the supply of moored floaters has been substantially reduced as older units have been retired and scrapped, while very few new rigs have been built, and there are no newbuilds on order to replace them. Demand is underpinned by a stronger focus on energy security and rising investment in offshore developments, including in benign-water regions such as India, Southeast Asia, Mexico and West Africa. High utilisation of moored floaters, together with limited availability of contract-ready units, is supporting higher day rates and longer contract terms.

About Dolphin Drilling AS

Dolphin Drilling AS, headquartered in Aberdeen, UK, is an owner and operator of a fleet of harsh-environment mid-water and deep-water semi-submersible drilling rigs capable of working worldwide, with a long track record of safe and efficient operations. About SPM Energy Shipping FZCO

SPM Energy Shipping FZCO (“SPM”), headquartered in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is a diversified ship owning and maritime operating company engaged in energy transportation, dry bulk shipping and offshore marine services.

Established in 2023 and supported by a group with maritime experience dating to 1994, the company serves international energy and commodity markets through an expanding fleet. SPM’s diversified portfolio includes nine tankers, comprising two Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs), four Very Large Gas Carriers (VLGCs), including two acquired through joint ventures, three Capesize bulk carriers and 20 offshore support vessels across its UAE and Indian operations.

Drawing upon the wider group’s more than three decades of maritime experience, SPM continues to strengthen and expand its presence across the international shipping and offshore energy sectors.
